item.text:
**Bottom line:** Mostly yes. Scholz did not try to stay in power by bypassing Germany’s constitutional transfer rules, and he ultimately accepted the path to early elections. The main negative is the coalition break with Lindner, which showed a serious coalition-commitment failure but not a refusal to leave office through lawful procedures.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Supportive | Regierungserklärung von Bundeskanzler Olaf Scholz | Bundesregierung | 2024-11-13 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/suche/regierungserklaerung-von-bundeskanzler-olaf-scholz-2320314 | Scholz said he had dismissed Lindner, linked the move to early elections, and asked for a confidence vote. This is evidence that he used the constitutional parliamentary route rather than trying to entrench himself. | 4B.8, 4B.1 |
| Supportive | Bundestag records Scholz’s Article 68 confidence procedure | Deutscher Bundestag | 2024-12-16 | https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw47-vertrauensfrage-1030198 | The Bundestag recorded the formal confidence procedure, Scholz’s loss of confidence, and the constitutional path to snap elections. This is direct evidence of respect for succession rules and constitutional transfer. | 4B.8, 4B.1 |
| Supportive | Bundestag confirms failed confidence vote and path to new elections | Deutscher Bundestag | 2024-12-16 | https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw51-de-vertrauensfrage-1033624 | The official record confirms the government’s managed exit into the election process, not an attempt to override it. | 4B.8, 4B.1 |
| Supportive | Scholz loses confidence vote, paving way for election | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-12-16 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/german-chancellor-scholz-loses-no-confidence-vote-paving-way-for-election-3773234 | Reuters reported the loss of confidence as the mechanism that opened the way for elections, reinforcing that Scholz accepted constitutional replacement. | 4B.8, 4B.1 |
| Supportive | Scholz urges calm debate over snap-election timing | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-11-08 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/german-voters-and-opposition-keep-heat-on-scholz-for-early-election-3710828 | Scholz denied trying to ram through his own agenda and said the timing should still allow a fair and democratic election. This supports respect for orderly succession rather than procedural manipulation. | 4B.8, 4B.1 |
| Counterweight | German coalition collapses after Scholz fires Lindner | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-11-06 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/explainergerman-coalition-collapses-what-comes-next-3706936 | Firing Lindner collapsed the coalition and triggered political chaos. This is strong evidence of broken coalition commitments and weakened governing continuity, though not of unconstitutional refusal to transfer power. | 4B.8 |
| Counterweight | The Guardian: Scholz loses confidence vote triggering early elections | The Guardian | 2024-12-16 | https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/dec/16/german-chancellor-olaf-scholz-loses-confidence-vote-triggering-early-elections | The Guardian reported that Scholz intentionally called a vote he expected to lose in order to trigger elections. That is still consistent with lawful transfer, but it confirms the chancellorship was ending under pressure rather than on a stable coalition basis. | 4B.8, 4B.1 |

**Search gap**
- Germany’s chancellorship does not operate with fixed term limits in the presidential sense, so the meaningful test here is constitutional transfer and parliamentary confidence, not a formal term-limit clock.
- I did not find evidence of Scholz trying to extend tenure past the constitutional process, block elections, or ignore succession rules.
- The clearest negative evidence is coalition rupture, not anti-constitutional entrenchment.
